g.text: Defenders embraced AI fast; attackers have barely begun
Left: major vendors shipping generative-AI security features,
of 34 tracked. Right: estimated annual AI spend, $, log scale
Left: cumulative count of the 34 security and platform vendors tracked, by the year each first shipped a substantive generative-AI
feature (a copilot or an autonomous agent, not legacy machine learning); median and 80% credible interval, allowing for uncertainty
about dates and about what counts as substantive. Right: a judgement Monte Carlo, median and 80% range. Defensive spend is the
generative-AI cyber-defence market (two research houses, ~$20bn in 2026); attacker spend is a generous guess, since bespoke
criminal tools proved thin wrappers or scams and crooks mostly jailbreak mainstream models. Order-of-magnitude, not a
Sources: author's vendor census (34 firms, dated to each vendor's first feature); Mordor Intelligence and Precedence Research
(defensive market); Abnormal Security and this article's evidence (attacker side); author's Bayesian models
